from.place: right adjoint commutes with direct sums: a perfect object is compact

title: Perfect complexes are compact in the quasi-coherent derived category
statement: Let X be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Every perfect object P [def-pc-perfect-complex] of D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X) [def-pc-derived-category] is compact: for every set I and family (K_i) in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X), the canonical map \bigoplus_{i\in I} \operatorname{Hom}(P,K_i) \to \operatorname{Hom}(P,\bigoplus_{i\in I}K_i) is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Let P^\vee be the dual of P supplied by [lem-pc-perfect-tensor-hom-duality]. For every M in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X), its first tensor-Hom isomorphism with A=\mathcal O_X and B=M (and P\otimes^L\mathcal O_X=P, as \mathcal O_X is a flat module in degree 0) identifies Hom(P,M) with Hom(\mathcal O_X,P^\vee\otimes^L M), naturally in M; in particular P^\vee\otimes^L M lies in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X).

Derived tensoring with the fixed complex P^\vee commutes with set-indexed direct sums. Choose a K-flat resolution of P^\vee using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]; the direct sum of the K_i, which exists in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}} by [lem-pc-derived-qcoh-direct-sums], is represented by the termwise direct sum of representative complexes by [lem-pc-derived-ambient-direct-sums]; form the total tensor complexes using [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. The termwise tensor products and the direct sums indexed by total degree commute, so the direct sum of the complexes P^\vee\otimes^L K_i is P^\vee\otimes^L(\bigoplus_i K_i), compatibly with the inclusions of the summands.

Let Y=\operatorname{Spec}(\mathbb Z) and let a:X\to Y be the structure morphism; it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated because X is. Since \mathcal O_Y is a flat module in degree 0, La^*\mathcal O_Y=\mathcal O_X, so by the adjunction [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-adjoint] Hom(\mathcal O_X,N)\cong Hom(\mathcal O_Y,Ra_*N) naturally in N. By [lem-pc-derived-direct-image-preserves-direct-sums], Ra_* maps D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X) to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y) and commutes with direct sums. By [lem-pc-affine-qcoh-derived-equivalence] with A=\mathbb Z, R\Gamma(Y,-) is an equivalence D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y)\to D(\mathbb Z) sending \mathcal O_Y to \mathbb Z; an equivalence preserves direct sums, so Hom(\mathcal O_Y,L)\cong Hom_{D(\mathbb Z)}(\mathbb Z,R\Gamma(Y,L))=H^0(R\Gamma(Y,L)) commutes with direct sums, because in D(\mathbb Z) direct sums are termwise and H^0 commutes with direct sums of abelian groups. Composing with Steps 1 and 2, Hom(P,-) is naturally isomorphic to a functor on D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X) whose canonical comparison map for direct sums is an isomorphism; by naturality the canonical map \bigoplus_i Hom(P,K_i)\to Hom(P,\bigoplus_i K_i) is an isomorphism, including for the empty family.
